questions.question: Q1(a). Angles between x-√3y = a and √3x-y = b.
questions.solution: m₁ = 1/√3, m₂ = √3. tanθ = (√3-1/√3)/(1+1) = (2/√3)/2 = 1/√3. Boxed θ = 30° (matches the printed key, book p398).

questions.solution: m₁ = -3/2, m₂ = 2/3; product -1. Boxed 90° (matches the printed key).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.13 Ex 13.2 Q1(b); book p397 = PDF p424 (vision read)

questions.question: Q1(c). Angle between 2x-3y+7 = 0 and 7x+4y-9 = 0.
questions.solution: m₁ = 2/3, m₂ = -7/4. tanθ = (2/3+7/4)/(1-7/6) = (29/12)/(-1/6) = -29/2. Acute angle arctan(29/2). [Print note: the key's 1c) tan⁻¹(±2/9) does not follow from these printed lines under either 3x- or 7x-reading (17/6 vs 29/2) — flagged as a key slip; the substitution-verified value from the zoom-confirmed lines is tan⁻¹(±29/2).]

questions.question: Q4. k so that 3x-ky-8 = 0 makes 45° with 3x+5y-17 = 0.
questions.solution: m₁ = 3/k, m₂ = -3/5. (3/k+3/5)/(1-9/5k) = ±1: +1 gives 15+3k = 5k-9, k = 12; -1 gives 15+3k = -5k+9, k = -3/4. Boxed k = 12 or -3/4 (matches the printed key).
